name: Media location metadata
plain: Lets the app read the GPS location stored inside photos.
meaning: Photo EXIF reveals where and when images were taken, including home and holiday locations.

android.note: Without it EXIF GPS is redacted for media the app reads (Android 10+).

ios.note: Location is returned with photo access; shares can strip location via share sheet Options.

limits.headline: Can see where your photos were taken, if you allow location info in media
limits.user_action: You tap Allow on the Location in media prompt, often in a gallery or editing app
can: See the GPS place saved inside photos, on Android once you allow it
Ask for the original photo with its location, not the hidden version
See photo locations on iPhone along with photo access
Use the place to sort photos on a map
cannot: See the location of Android photos without this permission; GPS is removed from the copy the app sees
Keep location in shared photos on iPhone if you pick Options and turn off Location
Track where you are now from photos alone
See photos you did not allow the app to open
limits.differs: On iPhone, location comes with photo access. On Android it is a separate permission.

story.what_it_is: Lets an app read the place stored inside your photos.

marketing.name: Media location
marketing.pitch: Developer guide: apps must ask separately to see the GPS location saved in photos.

story.for_you: A pop up asks to access location in your photos. If you allow it, the app can see where each photo was taken, which can show your home, work and trips.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to sort photos by place, build maps and tag albums. It is very sensitive because it puts a pin on your private life.

use_cases.example: A photo album app places your holiday pictures on a world map.
A social app suggests a place tag when you post a photo.
A photo editor shows the location data and offers to remove it before you share.
A privacy tool strips location from photos before you send them.
A real estate app reads where a photo was taken to check a listing is real.
A map app builds a heat map of places you have photographed.
An ad firm could use photo places to guess your home and work.

risks: Can leak when you share photos
story.android_note: Needs ACCESS_MEDIA_LOCATION on top of photo access.
story.ios_note: iOS apps with photo access can read location unless you share without it.

technical_bounds: iOS gives location with library access

history.change: EXIF GPS redacted unless ACCESS_MEDIA_LOCATION granted
